tools.name: find_mcp_servers
tools.description: Search canmyaiuse's live-checked directory of public MCP servers by capability, app or name (e.g. 'send invoices', 'postgres', 'web search'). Returns servers ranked by live status and trust grade, with auth type, tool count, remote URL and setup page. Only live servers by default.

tools.name: check_app
tools.description: Check whether an app or SaaS (e.g. Notion, HubSpot, Salesforce, Stripe) has an official MCP server, plus the best community servers, each with live status.

tools.name: get_mcp_server
tools.description: Full details for one MCP server by canmyaiuse id, registry name, remote URL or canmyaiuse page URL: live status, auth, trust grade, tool count, repo.

tools.name: mcp_ecosystem_status
tools.description: Current totals across the MCP ecosystem from canmyaiuse's latest sweep: servers listed, remote endpoints, live, down, OAuth, tools.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_mcp_servers, get_mcp_server · Public sink: find_mcp_servers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_mcp_servers, get_mcp_server · Public sink: find_mcp_servers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
